newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Bomb blast in Karachi wounds at least 11.
newsitem.headline: Bomb blast in Karachi wounds at least 11.

text.p: A bomb explosion jolted the business district of Pakistan's southern port city of Karachi on Wednesday, wounding at least 11 people.
The blast, which police said was caused by a time-bomb, followed one that wounded six people at a shopping centre in the Punjab provincial capital Lahore on Tuesday.
Doctors said they had treated 11 people for wounds from flying shards of glass and debris in the Karachi blast. About 17 other people suffered minor injuries, witnesses said.

Police had no word on the motive for the bomb, placed in a bag on the pavement outside the headquarters of the state-owned Pakistan Industrial Development Corporation, where several multinational companies have offices.
The bomb wrecked a usually crowded branch of the state-run National Bank of Pakistan, but exploded in the middle of the day when many office workers had gone for lunch or prayers.
Witnesses said the blast set off a hail of glass fragments falling from upper floors of the 14-storey building.
The bomb dug a small crater in the pavement outside the bank. Inside, broken furniture littered the premises and blood smeared the floor.
The explosion occurred ahead of the planned arrival in Karachi of ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto on Wednesday, but there was no immediate evidence of a link.
